cards.back: The right or opportunity to use or benefit from something; a way of entering or reaching a place. "Students need access to reliable internet for online learning." Common collocations: gain access, have access, access to information.

A person who is fully grown or has reached the legal age of maturity. "Every adult in the household is responsible for paying taxes." Common collocations: young adult, adult education, adult population.

A quantity of something, especially the total of a thing or things in number, size, or value. "The amount of waste produced by cities has increased dramatically." Common collocations: large amount, small amount, significant amount.

Occurring once every year; calculated over or covering a period of one year. "The company holds an annual meeting to review its performance." Common collocations: annual report, annual income, annual event.

To make a formal request for something such as a job or course; to be relevant or suitable. "She decided to apply for a scholarship at the university." Common collocations: apply for a job, apply a method, apply pressure.

A region or part of a town, country, or the world; a subject or range of activity. "The research focuses on the area of renewable energy." Common collocations: urban area, area of expertise, surrounding area.

To organize or make plans for something; to put things in a particular order. "We need to arrange a meeting with the project team." Common collocations: arrange a meeting, arrange in order, arrange for someone.

An effort to achieve or complete something, often without success; to try to do something. "His first attempt to pass the exam was unsuccessful." Common collocations: make an attempt, attempt to do, failed attempt.

Having knowledge or perception of a situation or fact; conscious of something. "Many people are not aware of the risks associated with poor diet." Common collocations: become aware, fully aware, aware of the problem.
The underlying support or foundation for an idea, argument, or process. "The theory was formed on the basis of extensive research." Common collocations: on the basis of, regular basis, daily basis.
Having the ability, fitness, or quality needed to do or achieve something. "She is capable of managing large teams effectively." Common collocations: capable of doing, highly capable, capable leader.

A class or division of people or things regarded as having particular shared characteristics. "The books are organized into different categories by subject." Common collocations: fall into a category, broad category, category of people.

Relating to chemistry or the interactions of substances; a distinct compound or substance. "Chemical pollution in rivers is a serious environmental concern." Common collocations: chemical reaction, chemical substance, chemical industry.

To join or merge two or more things together to form a single unit or produce a result. "The chef decided to combine traditional and modern cooking techniques." Common collocations: combine efforts, combine with, combine elements.

To share or exchange information, ideas, or feelings with others through speaking, writing, or other means. "It is essential to communicate clearly in a professional environment." Common collocations: communicate effectively, communicate with, communicate ideas.

Consisting of many different and connected parts; not easy to understand or analyse. "The human brain is an incredibly complex organ." Common collocations: complex issue, complex system, highly complex.

To focus all one's attention or mental effort on a particular object or activity. "It is difficult to concentrate in a noisy environment." Common collocations: concentrate on, concentrate efforts, hard to concentrate.

To organize and carry out an activity; the manner in which a person behaves. "The university will conduct a survey on student satisfaction." Common collocations: conduct research, conduct a survey, code of conduct.

To establish the truth or correctness of something previously believed or suspected. "The test results confirm that the treatment is effective." Common collocations: confirm a booking, confirm the findings, confirm the date.

A serious disagreement or argument; a prolonged armed struggle between groups or nations. "There is often a conflict between economic growth and environmental protection." Common collocations: armed conflict, conflict resolution, conflict of interest.

Occurring continuously over a period of time; remaining the same and not changing. "The constant noise from the construction site disturbed the residents." Common collocations: constant change, constant pressure, remain constant.

To build or make something, typically a building, road, or machine; to form an idea or theory. "The government plans to construct a new motorway by next year." Common collocations: construct a building, construct an argument, newly constructed.

A person who purchases goods and services for personal use. "Consumer demand for organic food has risen sharply in recent years." Common collocations: consumer goods, consumer spending, consumer protection.

The circumstances that form the setting for an event, statement, or idea. "You need to consider the historical context before making a judgment." Common collocations: in context, social context, out of context.

A written or spoken agreement that is intended to be enforceable by law; to decrease in size. "Both parties must sign the contract before work begins." Common collocations: sign a contract, contract agreement, breach of contract.

The state of being strikingly different from something else when compared side by side. "There is a sharp contrast between life in rural and urban areas." Common collocations: in contrast to, by contrast, sharp contrast.

Belonging to the present time; happening or being used now. "The current economic situation makes it difficult for graduates to find work." Common collocations: current situation, current trends, current affairs.

A formal discussion on a particular topic in which opposing arguments are presented. "There is an ongoing debate about the effects of social media on youth." Common collocations: public debate, heated debate, debate over.
A period of ten years. "Over the past decade, technology has transformed the way we communicate." Common collocations: past decade, over a decade, in recent decades.

To state or describe the exact nature or scope of something; to mark the boundary of. "It is important to clearly define the objectives of a research project." Common collocations: clearly define, define the term, define the scope.

To be controlled or determined by something; to rely on someone or something for support. "The success of the project will depend on sufficient funding." Common collocations: depend on, depend heavily, it depends.

Without being affected by; in spite of a particular condition or difficulty. "Despite the heavy rain, the outdoor event continued as planned." Common collocations: despite the fact, despite efforts, despite challenges.

To give shares of something out to a number of recipients; to spread over an area. "The charity aims to distribute food supplies to affected communities." Common collocations: distribute evenly, distribute resources, widely distributed.

A piece of written, printed, or electronic matter that provides information or evidence. "You must submit the required documents before the deadline." Common collocations: official document, document the process, legal document.

A component or part of something; a substance that cannot be broken down into simpler substances. "Trust is an essential element of any successful relationship." Common collocations: key element, essential element, element of surprise.

To give someone or something the authority or means to do something; to make possible. "The new software will enable employees to work more efficiently." Common collocations: enable access, enable people to, enable growth.

The strength and vitality required for sustained physical or mental activity; power derived from resources. "Many countries are investing in renewable energy sources." Common collocations: renewable energy, energy consumption, save energy.
Very large in size, quantity, or extent. "The project required an enormous amount of time and resources." Common collocations: enormous pressure, enormous impact, enormous potential.

To make certain that something will occur or be the case. "The government must ensure that all citizens have access to healthcare." Common collocations: ensure safety, ensure quality, ensure compliance.
With no part left out; whole; complete. "The entire population was affected by the water shortage." Common collocations: entire country, entire process, the entire time.

The necessary items for a particular purpose; tools or machinery needed for a specific activity. "The laboratory needs new equipment to carry out advanced experiments." Common collocations: medical equipment, safety equipment, piece of equipment.

Absolutely necessary; extremely important and indispensable. "Regular exercise is essential for maintaining good health." Common collocations: essential role, essential information, absolutely essential.

An approximate calculation or judgment of the value, number, or quantity of something. "According to recent estimates, the world population will reach 10 billion by 2050." Common collocations: rough estimate, estimate the cost, conservative estimate.

To inspect someone or something in detail to determine their nature or condition. "Scientists need to examine the data carefully before drawing conclusions." Common collocations: examine the evidence, closely examine, examine the impact.

To become or make larger or more extensive; to develop or elaborate on something. "The company plans to expand its operations into new markets." Common collocations: expand rapidly, expand the business, expand knowledge.

A person who is very knowledgeable about or skilful in a particular area. "The panel of experts discussed the future of artificial intelligence." Common collocations: expert opinion, expert advice, leading expert.

The centre of interest or activity; to concentrate attention or effort on something. "The report focuses on the impact of climate change on agriculture." Common collocations: focus on, main focus, shift focus.
Relating to the whole world; worldwide in scope. "Global warming is affecting weather patterns across every continent." Common collocations: global economy, global issue, on a global scale.
Important, serious, or significant; greater in size or importance. "Traffic congestion is a major problem in most capital cities." Common collocations: major role, major factor, major concern.

Clearly defined or identified; precise and particular. "The teacher gave specific instructions on how to complete the assignment." Common collocations: specific details, specific requirements, be more specific.
